Match Preview: Round 25 – Dolphins v Eels
The Dolphins return to Suncorp Stadium for their final home game of the regular season, looking to strengthen their grip on a top-four spot against the Eels on Friday night.
With their maiden finals berth secured, the Dolphins now have their sights set on earning a double chance in September as the regular season enters its final three rounds.
The Eels head to Brisbane sitting 13th on the ladder, but arrive off an upset win over the Cowboys and will provide another challenge for the fourth-placed Dolphins.
The two sides have met three times since the Dolphins entered the competition, with the Dolphins claiming two victories. Their most recent meeting came in Round 10 last season, when the Dolphins secured a 20-16 victory at the Eels’ home ground.
Friday night will also mark a milestone for Selwyn Cobbo, who is set to play his 100th NRL game.
It will be a significant night for Jamayne Isaako, Kodi Nikorima, Jake Averillo and Ray Stone, who are all set to play their final regular-season home game for the Dolphins.
Suncorp Stadium has become a happy hunting ground for the Dolphins, who head into Round 25 having won their past seven games at the venue. Isaako has also crossed for 10 tries in his past eight appearances at Suncorp.

Two experienced Origin forwards will go head-to-head in the middle when Tom Gilbert takes on Junior Paulo.

Taking care of business
In a tricky road trip to face the Sea Eagles, the Dolphins did what was required in their 22-0 victory. Hardly exhibiting relentless pressure, the Dolphins will be most pleased by the fact that their defence was resolute and wasn’t cracked over 80 minutes. They strangled their opponents by missing just 26 tackles and allowing only 1 line break. This meant that they could build pressure with their attack; with 51% possession and a 74% completion rate, they averaged 9.9m per carry and made 672 PCM’s. Spirited and determined
The Eels caused a huge upset with their 32-30 home victory over the Cowboys. Expected to struggle against a superior opponent, the Eels failed to play to the predicted script of the match. They gave themselves every chance of performing well by completing at 90% with 52% possession, running for 10.5m per carry, making 642 PCM’s, and creating 7 line breaks. They’re improving their ability to ‘strangle’ teams out of a contest and raising to a higher intensity should be a focus for them ahead of this match. Despite being resilient in recent weeks, the Eels are about to find out the difference between them and a real Top 8 team. NRL Casualty Ward: Mitchell eyes comeback; Surgery for Doueihi, Walsh
South Sydney star Latrell Mitchell is in the mix to return from a nerve injury that has kept him sidelined since Round 11 for Saturday's showdown with the Warriors.
The centre has missed 11 games with the injury but has been named in the extended squad for this weekend's match at Accor Stadium.
Mitchell trained on Monday and has been running more freely as he builds up to a highly-anticipated return.
The Rabbitohs have lost Adam Elliott to a groin injury, with the veteran expected to miss two to three weeks with a strained adductor.
Meanwhile, Warriors halfback Luke Metcalf will miss the remainder of the regular season after suffering a hamstring injury in last week's win over Brisbane.
"The timeline for him will be deep into the finals but you never know," coach Andrew Webster said on Thursday.
"I think this is probably the most optimistic I've seen him when he knows he's got a plan and when he knows he wants to attack something."
With Te Maire Martin at least another week away from returning from a hamstring injury, rookie Luke Hanson will step into the halves for Saturday's clash with the Rabbitohs.
"We want to make sure we get it right but Te Maire is progressing well," Webster said.
Wests Tigers halfback Adam Doueihi will undergo season-ending surgery that will rule him out of Lebanon's World Cup campaign.
The playmaker dislocated his shoulder in a Round 9 loss to the Sharks and initially delayed surgery in an attempt to kickstart the Tigers finals campaign.
The 28-year-old returned to the field in Round 17 but fresh scans have shown Doueihi requires immediate surgery, with the halfback to go under the knife later this week.
"New scans on Adam's shoulder have showed the time has come to have his reconstruction done. This gives him enough time to be ready for the start of the 2027 season," Wests Tigers head of high performance Peter Moussa said.
Meanwhile, Tigers five-eighth Latu Fainu has suffered a low-grade hamstring injury at training. Fainu was set to return this week after serving a three-game suspension, but will now be sidelined for 1-2 weeks with his latest injury.
In positive news, Sunia Turuva has been named on the six-man bench despite suffering a knee injury last week, while Alex Twal is set to return after missing Round 24 due to illness.
The Roosters will also welcome back James Tedesco from an ankle injury for Sunday's clash against the Tigers at Allianz Stadium.
The Melbourne Storm will welcome back Harry Grant from a hamstring strain for Thursday's clash with the Panthers.
The hooker suffered the injury in the Round 21 loss to the Rabbitohs and is on track to return this week alongside centre Jack Howarth (shoulder) and forward Alec MacDonald (concussion).
Less positive news for Jahrome Hughes , who remains sidelined with a hamstring injury.
Mixed news on the injury front for Penrith, with gun centre Casey McLean back on deck from a broken hand, however Paul Alamoti has been ruled out with a hamstring injury.
Broncos superstar Reece Walsh has had surgery on his ankle and is facing an eight-week recovery time.

items.title: Dolphins cult hero makes call on future after persistent injury battle - Zero Tackle
items.snippet: Dolphins cult hero makes call on future after persistent injury battle    Zero Tackle
items.body_excerpt:
Dolphins forward Ray Stone has confirmed he will retire from the NRL at the end of the 2026 season, bringing an end to a career that has been defined by toughness and a battle against persistent injuries.
The 29-year-old has played more than 100 NRL games since making his debut with the Parramatta Eels in 2018, before becoming a key part of the Dolphins' inaugural squad.
Stone was the second-ever player signed by the expansion club ahead of their entry into the competition in 2023, helping establish the foundations of the Dolphins' playing group.
SYDNEY, AUSTRALIA - MARCH 11: Ray Stone runs during a Parramatta Eels NRL training session at Old Saleyards Reserve on March 11, 2019, in Sydney, Australia. (Photo by Matt King/Getty Images)
However, a series of significant injuries have taken their toll on the forward, with Stone ultimately deciding to call time on his career at the conclusion of the season.
He suffered an ACL injury towards the back end of 2022 before enduring AC joint injuries throughout last season.
Dolphins coach Kristian Woolf made special mention of Stone's toughness at last year's presentation, highlighting the veteran's willingness to battle through games despite his shoulder injury.
Stone has also dealt with a neck injury this season, only returning to the field last week in the Dolphins' win over Manly.
His final season will see him remain part of a significant moment in the club's short history, with the Dolphins having secured their first finals appearance since entering the NRL in 2023.
Dolphins chief executive Terry Reader paid tribute to Stone's contribution to the club and his standing among the fanbase.
WAGGA WAGGA, AUSTRALIA - APRIL 29: Ray Stone of the Dolphins in action during the round nine NRL match between the Canberra Raiders and Dolphins at McDonald's Park on April 29, 2023 in Wagga Wagga, Australia. (Photo by Mark Nolan/Getty Images)
"There is no doubt that Ray has come to our club and entrenched himself as a real hard man and one of our fans' favourite players," said Dolphins' chief executive Terry Reader.
"He will forever hold a place in our history as the second NRL player signed by the club, and he has returned that favour by playing every game in a tough and uncompromising manner.
"We will always be thankful to Ray for the effort he has put in for the Dolphins and wish him and his young family all the best for the future."
Stone will now look to finish his career on a high, with the Dolphins set to make their first appearance in the NRL finals since joining the competition.

Raiders vs Broncos Preview & Betting Tips: NRL Round 25 2026
August 20 th 2026, 3:36pm , By: Ben Bridge
Friday Night Football at GIO Stadium has far more riding on it than the respective ladder positions suggest, as the Raiders host Brisbane in a matchup loaded with desperation, emotion, and a little revenge. Canberra’s finals hopes remain incredibly faint, but they are still alive. Wins over Brisbane and North Queensland, combined with their Round 26 bye, could get the Raiders to 30 competition points, and leave them praying other results fall their way. Brisbane, meanwhile, have endured one of the worst premiership defences in modern NRL history and are now fighting simply to avoid an unthinkable wooden spoon.
Then there is Josh Papali’i. Friday night will be the Canberra legend’s final home appearance, with GIO Stadium even being temporarily transformed into “Papa’s House” for the occasion. Papali’i has been promoted into the starting front row, and you can guarantee the Raiders faithful will turn this into one of the most emotional home games of the season.
My numbers are not miles away from the current spread, but the circumstances push me toward Canberra. With the Broncos broken, Reece Walsh gone for the season and the Raiders needing a win, I’ll take Canberra -10.5.
Raiders vs Broncos Prediction & Tips: 2026 NRL Round 25
Raiders Refuse to Let Season Die
Canberra looked like a team whose finals hopes were virtually finished heading into last week’s trip to Sharks Stadium, yet they produced one of their gutsiest performances of the season to upset Cronulla 24-20. Against a Sharks side sitting firmly in the top 4 conversation, the Raiders absorbed an early 8-0 deficit, fought their way to an 18-14 halftime lead and then survived a frantic final quarter to keep their season alive.
Joseph Tapine delivered the decisive moment after the Sharks had regained a 20-18 advantage, powering through five defenders to score underneath the posts in the 57th minute. From there, Canberra defended their lead despite Cronulla receiving several opportunities to steal the game late.
It was exactly the type of performance Ricky Stuart would have wanted after the Raiders’ form had again become inconsistent. Canberra have enough attacking talent through Kaeo Weekes, Ethan Strange, Ethan Sanders, Matthew Timoko and Xavier Savage, but their success still starts with the middle. Tapine, Papalii, Zac Hosking and Ata Mariota must generate the field position that allows the young spine to play with freedom.
Morgan Smithies’ failed HIA against Cronulla rules him out this week, forcing Mariota to lock, while Corey Horsburgh returns through the interchange. Simi Sasagi is also back from a shoulder problem, strengthening the centres.
The emotional factor cannot be ignored. Papali’i starts in his final match at GIO Stadium, and Canberra have averaged 35 points across their past four home games. If there is one night where this Raiders side should produce maximum effort for 80 minutes, this is it.
Broncos Hit Rock Bottom in Premiership Defence
Brisbane’s extraordinary collapse continued last Saturday when the Warriors humiliated them 40-6 at Suncorp Stadium. The Broncos trailed 20-0 at halftime and did not score until Xavier Willison crossed in the 64th minute, by which point New Zealand had already put 36 points on the board.
The statistics around Brisbane’s season are becoming almost unbelievable for the defending premiers. They have now lost 12 of their past 13 games, and they are staring down the worst fall from grace by a premiership winning side since Western Suburbs went from premiers to wooden spooners in 1963. Brisbane are now fighting simply to avoid finishing last.
Things somehow got worse against the Warriors when Reece Walsh suffered a syndesmosis injury that has ended his season. Hayze Perham takes over at fullback this week, while Ben Hunt returns to halfback for the first time since Round 18 and Tom Duffy drops to the bench.
